runbook: R-18 / R-19 (fresh independent oracle; evidence tree = `git archive HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md` only)
old_value: The represented mechanic changes defense, not outgoing TDD.
new_value: Every declared family on this item is a defence: the represented mechanic changes durability, not outgoing TDD.
what_had_to_be_checked: Core claim (shared by both strings): the coverage entry's represented mechanic is a defensive mechanic and contributes nothing to outgoing total damage dealt (TDD).
Added claim (new string only, the sole discriminator): EVERY declared family on that item is a defence - i.e. the item declares no effect family that feeds outgoing damage.

identification_of_the_item.constraint: The evidence tree contains no golden baseline and no scenario definition (data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json holds 22 scenarios, none for Syndra), so the item behind item_coverage[0] is not directly readable from data/. It was narrowed by construction instead.
narrowing: The scenario is a Summoner's-Rift coupled fight, so item_source legality applies: only items with modes['classic sr 5v5'] and no champion restriction can be held (data/README.md, 'Item source fields').
The entry is an AP-carry (Syndra) item whose represented mechanic is defence-only and unpriceable as a damage source.

Scan of data/items.json for SR-legal, tier-3, AP-carrying items whose complete passives[].branches / active[].branches text contains no damage/on-hit/penetration/stat-offense language yields exactly: Zhonya's Hourglass (Time Stop), Shurelya's Battlesong (move speed), Cryptbloom (heal), Moonstone Renewer (heal). Of these only Zhonya's Hourglass is a defence (durability) mechanic. Banshee's Veil (Annul spell shield) is the only other SR-legal AP item whose sole declared effect is purely defensive (it fell out of the keyword scan only because its cooldown clause contains the word 'damage').
Conclusion: the item is Zhonya's Hourglass, with Banshee's Veil the only alternative candidate. Both were verified independently below and both give the same verdict.

candidate_A.wiki_text_quoted: Time Stop - "Put yourself in {{tip|stasis (buff)|stasis}} for {{fd|2.5}} seconds, rendering you {{tip|untargetable}} and {{tip|invulnerable}} for the duration but also unable to move, declare [[basic attack]]s, cast [[champion ability|abilities]], use [[summoner spell]]s, or [[active ability items|activate items]]."
derivation: The effect text declares no damage term of any kind: no flat/ratio damage row, no on-hit, no penetration, no amplifier. Outgoing-damage contribution of the mechanic = 0.
The effect text declares untargetable + invulnerable for 2.5 s: it removes incoming damage entirely for the window, i.e. it is a durability (defence) mechanic.

The item declares exactly ONE effect (passives[] is empty, active[] has one entry), so the set of declared effect families is a singleton, and that family is defensive (per data/item-atoms/3157.json the atoms sourced from 'active:Time Stop' are crowd-control-mobility.stasis and damage.resistance-mitigation - both defensive; the remaining atoms stats.ability-power / stats.armor carry provenance evidence 'stats', i.e. stat lines, not declared effect families).
Therefore both the core claim AND the universal 'every declared family is a defence' claim are TRUE for this item.

candidate_B.wiki_text_quoted: Annul - "Grants a {{tip|spell shield}} that blocks the next hostile ability (40 second cooldown, timer restarts upon taking damage from champions)."
derivation: Blocks an incoming hostile ability; no outgoing damage term. Mechanic contribution to outgoing TDD = 0; it is a durability mechanic.

Exactly one declared effect (single passive, no active); its atoms in data/item-atoms/3102.json sourced from 'passive:Annul' are heal-shield.shield / heal-shield.shield-magic / heal-shield.heal-and-shield-power - all defensive. Stat atoms again carry evidence 'stats'.
Both claims TRUE for this item as well.

counter_candidate_ruled_out.why_it_would_have_broken_the_new_string: It declares TWO passives - Awe ("Grants {{as|ability power}} equal to {{as|2% '''bonus''' mana}}") and Lifeline ("...you first gain a {{tip|shield}}...absorbs damage equal to {{as|18% '''maximum''' mana}}"). Awe is an ability-power grant, which does raise outgoing TDD, so 'every declared family on this item is a defence' would be FALSE there.
counter_candidate_ruled_out.why_it_is_not_the_item: Its defensive family is a shield - a priceable utility outcome that the utility_outcomes ledger models rather than excludes - and it is not among the SR-legal AP items whose complete declared effect set is defence-only. The excluded-mechanic reason applies to unpriceable durability mechanics (stasis / spell shield), not to shields.

independent_computation.result: For the item that can carry this coverage reason in an SR Syndra build, the represented mechanic is defence-only AND the item declares no non-defensive effect family. The new string is true and strictly more specific than the old; the old string is also true but weaker (it says nothing about the other declared families, i.e. it does not establish that the item has no separately-priceable offensive mechanic).

No formula in the document bears on this leaf: it states identities for resistance mitigation, the coupled participant-timeline score f(S), and the BIS search; it contains no item-coverage / defence-family identity. Checked lines 247-264 (sigmoid mitigation family), 350-400 (coupled score + optimizer), 455-480 (engine family audit table). Cited here as a negative result, not as support.

caveats: The scenario definition and the golden baseline are outside the permitted evidence tree, so the item behind item_coverage[0] was narrowed by SR legality + defence-only-effect scan rather than read directly. Both surviving candidates (Zhonya's Hourglass, Banshee's Veil) yield the same verdict, so the verdict does not depend on which of the two it is.

Reading of 'declared family': the sentence's own colon binds the quantifier to the represented mechanic ('...: the represented mechanic changes durability'), and the cache classifies stat lines with provenance evidence 'stats' separately from effect-sourced atoms. Under a stat-inclusive reading, Zhonya's 105 AP does raise Syndra's outgoing TDD - but that stat is priced by the stats layer, and neither the old nor the new string denies it. Only the effect-family reading is consistent with either string.

Both strings share one modelling simplification, so it does not separate them: the quoted Time Stop text says the wielder is 'unable to ... declare basic attacks, cast abilities', so inside a bounded fight window the mechanic can REDUCE the wielder's own outgoing TDD. Neither string models that; both assert only that the mechanic is not a SOURCE of outgoing TDD, which is correct.
verdict_rationale: Both strings assert the same true core fact. The new string's only additional assertion - that every declared family on the item is a defence - is independently confirmed from the cached wiki text: the item declares exactly one effect, and that effect (stasis/invulnerability for Zhonya's; spell shield for Banshee's) is wholly defensive, with the effect-sourced atoms falling entirely in defensive families. The new value is therefore correct and strictly better evidenced than the old.
